name: Trdat of Iberia
summary:
Trdat of Iberia (trdat-of-iberia) was a prominent king (mepe) of the Chosroid Dynasty who ruled Iberia from approximately 394 to 406 CE. A key figure in the region's history, Trdat played a crucial role in shaping Iberian politics and culture during this period.

Trdat's reign was marked by significant events, including his consolidation of power, religious conversions, and strategic alliances with neighboring kingdoms. His legacy continued to influence Iberia long after his death, leaving behind a lasting impact on the region's history and identity.

As one of the last Chosroid kings, Trdat's significance extends beyond his own reign, as he represented a pivotal moment in the transition from the Classical to Late Antiquity periods. His story serves as a testament to the enduring power of regional leaders in shaping the course of human events.

The 406 CE date of Trdat's death is often cited as marking the end of an era in Iberian history, with his passing leading to a period of instability and power struggles among neighboring kingdoms. Despite this, Trdat's legacy remains a powerful symbol of regional resilience and cultural continuity in the face of shifting global powers.
